title: 2014-2015 Jeep Cherokee, 2015 Chrysler 200 / Renegade / ProMaster City nine-speed (948TE): rough shifts, warranty extension X80, TCM flash 21-019-17
summary: FCA extended the warranty on early nine-speed automatics (948TE, plus the 9HP48 in the 3.6L Chrysler 200) to 6 years / 100,000 miles for transmission replacement (X80). Its TCM software update 21-019-17 addresses a list of transmission codes, a hard-to-get 3-2 downshift on grades, and garage-shift and coast-down bumps. Before blaming the transmission for shudder or gear-ratio codes on an AWD vehicle, FCA's STAR case says to check that all four tires are within 1/8 in of the same circumference.

specs.name: X80 warranty extension
specs.value: Transmission replacement covered 6 years from in-service date or 100,000 miles (U.S.)
specs.note: Counted from the in-service date, so 2014-2015 vehicles have aged out by now; it matters for repair history and goodwill requests.

specs.name: X80 vehicles
specs.value: 2014-2015 Cherokee (2.4L or 3.2L, 948TE); 2015 Chrysler 200 (2.4L 948TE, 3.6L 9HP48); 2015 Renegade (2.4L 948TE); 2015 ProMaster City (2.4L 948TE)

specs.name: TCM flash 21-019-17 Rev. A codes (2015 Cherokee)
TCM flash 21-019-17 Rev. A codes (2015 Chrysler 200)
Tire circumference match (AWD shudder / gear ratio codes)
specs.value: All four within 1/8 in of each other

steps.text: Check that the TCM has the latest software. Bulletin 21-019-17 Rev. A (also rapid response transmittal 14-094) reflashes 2015 Cherokee and 200 TCMs with wiTECH for the listed codes, a hard or missing 3-2 downshift on grades, and garage-shift and coast-down bumps.
For shudder, binding or gear-ratio codes, set tire pressures to the door placard first.

Measure each tire's circumference with a cloth tape at the center of the tread. If they aren't within 1/8 in of each other, find the cause (alignment, worn suspension, mixed brands, missed rotations) and replace tires as needed.
Road test and confirm all four wheel speed sensors read the same, and that the programmed tire size and axle ratio match what's on the vehicle.

body: The STAR case is a general FCA write-up covering many transmissions and years, not only the nine-speed. It's here because mismatched tires on an AWD Cherokee produce the same shudder and gear-ratio complaints. FCA states that STAR cases don't authorize warranty repairs.
